# Adding a game {.unnumbered}

The book is built from `games/`, one file per game. Nothing else is written by
hand: the chapter, the PGN, the place in the chronology, the era it falls in,
the contents and the list of sources are all derived. Adding a game is one
file and one command.

```bash
make new SLUG=1963-byrne-fischer   # writes games/1963-byrne-fischer.yml
$EDITOR games/1963-byrne-fischer.yml
make all                           # replays it, rebuilds, renders
make check                         # the audits
```

The file name is the slug, which is also the chapter's URL, so it is worth
choosing: year first keeps `games/` in the order the book publishes them.

## The record

```yaml
title: The Game of the Century      # how the game is known
white: Donald Byrne
black: Bobby Fischer
result: "0-1"                       # 1-0, 0-1 or 1/2-1/2
date: 1956-10-17                    # 1956, 1956-10 or 1956-10-17
event: Third Rosenwald Trophy tournament
site: Marshall Chess Club, New York, United States
opening: Grünfeld Defence
eco: D92

why: >                              # one sentence; the chapter's subtitle
  Fischer was thirteen.

summary: >                          # a paragraph for the head of the chapter
  Donald Byrne was an international master...

moves: |
  1. Nf3 Nf6 2. c4 g6 3. Nc3 Bg7 4. d4 O-O 5. Bf4 d5 6. Qb3 dxc4
  7. Qxc4 c6 8. e4 Nbd7 9. Rd1 Nb6 10. Qc5 Bg4 11. Bg5? Na4!!

sources:
  - title: The Game of the Century (Wikipedia)
    url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_of_the_Century_(chess)
    note: move list, tournament details

annotations:
  - at: 17b                         # 17w, 17b, or 17 for White
    by: Jonathan Rowson             # whose judgement, if it is not this book's
    text: >
      Rowson called it one of the most powerful moves of all time.
```

`title`, `white`, `black`, `result`, `date` and `moves` are required, and so is
at least one source: a game whose moves cannot be traced to a published record
does not go in the book. Everything else is optional. An unknown field is an
error rather than being ignored, because a misspelt key is easier to catch at
build time than to find in a rendered page.

Two more fields exist for the unusual cases: `circa: true`, for a date that is
a tradition rather than a record, and `orientation: black`, which turns the
board round for a game that is about what Black did. `start_fen` publishes a
position rather than a game from the first move.

## The moves

Written as they are played, in algebraic notation. Move numbers are ignored,
`0-0` is read as castling, and `!`, `?`, `!!` and `?!` after a move are kept
as the annotator's marks and shown apart from the notation. Variations in
brackets are refused: the book publishes the game as played, and an alternative
line belongs in an annotation where it can be read.

Every move is replayed on a board when the record is read. An illegal move
stops the build and names the game, the move number and the position:

```
1 game(s) will not build:
  games/1851-anderssen-kieseritzky.yml: move 6... 'Qh7': illegal san: 'Qh7'
    position: rnb1kb1r/p1pp1ppp/5n2/1B6/4Pp1q/5N2/PPPP2PP/RNBQ1K1R b kq - 2 6
```

## The notes

`at: 18w` is White's eighteenth move, `at: 18b` Black's reply. The build puts
each note in the box under the board, where it appears as the board reaches
that move, and as a comment on that move in the published PGN. Several notes
can point at the same move; they are shown in the order they are written.

`by` is whose judgement the note reports. Leave it empty for a note written for
this book. Fill it in whenever the assessment belongs to someone else, and list
the source it was read in with the game. That convention is the only thing
keeping the book's own opinions distinguishable from other people's.

## Where the game lands

Nothing says where a chapter goes. The games are sorted by date, and grouped
into parts by the year: the eras are a table at the top of
`scripts/build/records.py`, and a game added to `games/` takes its place in the
contents without any list being edited. The timeline, the counts on it and the
list of sources are all rewritten on every build.
